newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coles sells Sydney site for A$25.8 mln.
newsitem.headline: Coles sells Sydney site for A$25.8 mln.

text.p: Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer Ltd said on Friday it had sold the stratum air rights for a proposed hotel and apartment development in Sydney for A$25.8 million.
Coles said in a statement the hotel purchaser was MCH Trustee, a 60/40 joint venture between Raffles Holdings and Koala Investments.
Raffles Holdings is a subsidiary of DBS Land, while Koala Investments is part of the Singapore government-controlled Temasek Holdings.
The apartments' purchaser is Tower Apartments Pty Ltd, an investment company managed by merchant banker Grant Samuel Property Services, who would oversee project development.
Coles said the A$25.8 million purchase price would be paid on deferred terms, with part-payment made next May and the balance on completion of the project in mid-1999.
The tower, over the site of the Grace Bros store in Sydney's cntral business district, would comprise a 15-storey, 366-room luxury hotel and 100 residential apartments over 11 floors.
The hotel would be managed by Raffles under its Merchant Court brand and would be aimed at business travellers, the statement said.
A retail section, known as Sydney Central Plaza, would comprise the redeveloped Grace Bros store and 85 specialty shops.
Retail redevelopment began in February last year and was due to be completed in the second half of 1998.
